abort.single_instance_allowed: Home in Review is already set up.

user.title: Home in Review
user.description: A monthly report of your home, made from your energy dashboard, local weather and indoor sensors. Reports appear in the sidebar.

data_description.backfill_months: Earlier months are generated in the background from long-term statistics. The suggestion covers all of last year and this year so far, so both year reviews start complete. Use 0 to skip.

settings.title: Home in Review options
settings.description: Open a section to change it. Saving closes this window.

data.notify_services: Notify when a report is ready
data.admin_only: Only administrators can view the reports

data_description.report_day: Last month's report is made on this day.
data_description.year_start_month: January for a calendar year; for example July for a heating season or the month your energy contract starts.
data_description.admin_only: Off: every Home Assistant user in the household can open them (they show energy use, costs and when rooms are used).
data_description.default_theme: Used until a viewer picks another theme at the end of a report (remembered per browser).

data.max_hourly_kwh: Largest plausible grid use per hour
data.heat_pump_heat_sensor: Heat delivered by the heat pump
data.gas_base_per_day: Gas for hot water and cooking per day

data_description.fixed_costs_daily: Optional, including tax: standing charges and grid fees minus a fixed daily tax credit (may be negative).
data_description.fixed_costs_monthly: Optional, including tax. Use a negative amount for a fixed tax credit.
data_description.max_hourly_kwh: Meter jumps above this per hour are treated as glitches. Roughly your connection: 3 × 25 A ≈ 17 kWh, 3 × 35 A ≈ 24 kWh, 1 × 40 A ≈ 9 kWh.
data_description.heat_pump_devices: Any brand: one or more energy sensors (the heat pump's own integration, a kWh meter or smart plug, e.g. compressor and backup heater). Adds a heat pump slide with electricity per degree day.
data_description.heat_pump_heat_sensor: Optional: energy sensors for heat delivered (many brands report heating and hot water separately; choose both). Adds the COP.
data_description.gas_base_per_day: Optional, in your gas unit (e.g. 0.4 m³). Splits gas into heating and the rest. Empty: estimated per month from how gas use follows the degree days.
data_description.gas_use: Only hot water and cooking: for a home heated otherwise (e.g. a heat pump); all gas then counts as hot water and cooking. Otherwise heating and hot water are split per month from how gas follows the weather, or measured from the boiler's status below.
data_description.gas_hot_water_active: Optional: the boiler's hot-water status (e.g. OpenTherm). With this and/or the heating status, gas is split per hour from what the boiler was doing instead of being estimated from the weather. A sensor adds up the hours; it is used once it has measured at least 7 days of a month.
data_description.gas_heating_active: Optional: the boiler's central-heating status (binary sensor), or a thermostat (counts as heating while it reports heating).

data_description.excluded_areas: Sensors in these areas are left out of the indoor climate. Empty = count everything.
data_description.outdoor_sensor: Optional. Any temperature sensor with history; replaces the modelled temperature.
data_description.use_open_meteo: Free weather archive for your area (location rounded to ~10 km). Off: only your own sensors, without normals or sunshine.
data_description.rain_sensor: Optional. A precipitation sensor that counts up (total); replaces the modelled rainfall.
data_description.degree_day_base: Optional. Days with an average temperature below this count as heating days. Empty: 18 °C (65 °F). To compare with another service, use the same value it uses.
data_description.degree_days_weighted: November to February count ×1.1, March and October ×1.0, April to September ×0.8: the weighting commonly used in the Netherlands to compare gas use. Earlier months are updated automatically.

car.name: Car

data_description.teslamate_home_geofence: Used to count charging at home. Empty: a geofence called Home (or its translation).
data_description.evcc_url: Optional, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:7070. Adds charging sessions, cost and solar share per vehicle.

car.description: Any car: choose its odometer (from the car's own integration) and your charger's energy sensor. Richer sources, used first when filled in: TeslaMate (trips, Wh/km; Grafana URL and a token of a Viewer service account) and evcc (charging sessions, cost, solar share).

ai.name: AI summary

data_description.ai_instructions: Optional, e.g. the tone of voice or who lives in the house.

ai.description: Optional: a short written summary at the start of each report, by your own AI Task entity. Only the report's figures are sent.

tile_add.title: Add your own figure
tile_add.description: Shown on a 'Your figures' slide, compared with earlier months.

data_description.run_hours: For runs only, optional: a longer block counts as several runs (e.g. 3 h for a dishwasher). Runs are counted from the hourly average power; pauses of up to 2 hours belong to the same run.

error.invalid_url: Enter a valid http:// or https:// address without query or fragment.
error.url_credentials: Don't put a user name or password in the address; use the token field.
error.https_required: The token would be sent unencrypted to an address outside your network; use https://.
error.teslamate_incomplete: Fill in both the Grafana address and the token, or neither.

options.ha: Home Assistant (follows your Home Assistant theme)

generate.name: Generate report
generate.description: Collects (or re-collects) the report for one month.

month.name: Month
month.description: As YYYY-MM. Defaults to last month.

backfill.name: Backfill reports
backfill.description: Generates reports for earlier months in the background.

months.name: Months
months.description: How many months to look back. Default: back to the start of last year (in your year review's months).

overwrite.name: Overwrite
overwrite.description: Also re-make months that already have a report (after an update or a change in options).
